subject: Implementing random effect in zero-inflated neg. binomial model

messages.author: 7f2609deedcb09b0
messages.subject: Implementing random effect in zero-inflated neg. binomial model
parts:
Hello all,

I'm building a model and wish to apply a random effect to all of the independent variables (the "combo" variable is the random effect). I have specified two models through BRMS, and I'm not sure why they work different. They're listed below:


fit_zinb1 <- brm(camShot ~ (race + cam + race*cam | combo) + (log(racePop+1)), 
                 data = countyPoisson, family = zero_inflated_negbinomial()) 

fit_zinb2 <- brm(camShot ~ race + cam + race*cam + (1 | combo) + (log(racePop+1)), 
                       data = countyPoisson, family = zero_inflated_negbinomial())


When I run the first model and print a summary, the output only lists group-level effects (a bunch of standard deviations and correlations amongst the independent variables). When I run the second model, the output lists population-level AND group-level effects. Can anyone shed light on why I'm getting such different results between the two models?

Thanks in advance!
-Hope

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Implementing random effect in zero-inflated neg. binomial model
parts:
Hi Hope,

both models are completely different. The first model fits, as you point out, only random effects. Since they are centerd around zero, they are more or less meaningless without a corresponding fixed effect. Accordingly, you almost certainly want

fit_zinb3 <- brm(camShot ~ race + cam + race*cam + (race + cam + race*cam | combo) + (log(racePop+1)),
                 data = countyPoisson, family = zero_inflated_negbinomial())


The second model has the fixed effects, but only a random intercept: (1 | combo).

If you want race, combo and their interaction to vary across combo, fit_zinb3 ist the way to go.

Best,
Paul

P.S. You can simplify the model specification without altering the output by writing

fit_zinb3 <- brm(camShot ~ race*cam + (race*cam | combo) + (log(racePop+1)),
                 data = countyPoisson, family = zero_inflated_negbinomial())

as race*cam is expanded to race + cam + race:cam anyway (default R formula parsing)

parts:
When I run a zero-inflated model through the pscl package, the output gives estimates for the count part of the model and the zero part. It looks like brms gives only the count part. Is there any way to see estimates for the chances of an excess zero for each parameter?

Thanks!

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Implementing random effect in zero-inflated neg. binomial model
parts:
To also model the zero-inflation probability using the same predictors, go for:

fit_zinb3 <- brm(bf(camShot ~ race*cam + (race*cam | combo) + (log(racePop+1)),
                    zi ~ race*cam + (race*cam | combo) + (log(racePop+1))),
data = countyPoisson, family = zero_inflated_negbinomial())
You may use other predictors as well.
